newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee seen down after Tuesday sell-off.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee seen down after Tuesday sell-off.

text.p: Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Coffee is likely to attack lower support levels after its 10 per cent fall on Tuesday, analysts said.
Traders said benchmark September coffee was due to open unchanged on figures, but expected to see a fall on follow-through from Tuesday's sell off.
Coffee looked likely to attack the support it built up earlier this year around $1,500, according to Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis.
If it breached that level, than it could face a return to lower levels seen last year.
On the upside it faced a lot of supply coming in above $1,700. "It's more likely to come down," she said.

"London should be due a bounce after the rout yesterday, but traders will probably wait until they see if the U.S. collapses in the same manner after the GCA figures showed a 139,000 bag rise in stocks in June," brokers GNI said.
Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in June by 139,000 60-kg bags, to 2,116,000 bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported.

Traders and analysts said the increase was mostly within expectations, with most estimates coming in at plus or minus 100,000 bags, although some market participants had predicted a build of up to 200,000 bags.
New York coffee futures ended down on Tuesday as speculative selling drove prices to more than three-month lows, dealers said.
They added, however, that turnover was unimpressive and prices were confined to a relatively narrow range as many market participants awaited the GCA data.
No damaging cold was in sight for the next five days in Brazil's coffee regions, independent forecaster Weather Services Corporation said on Wednesday.

Brazilian domestic coffee roasters were finding it easier to buy the coffees they wanted in the quantity they wanted as supply from the harvest was picking up, the Sao Paulo State Coffee Industry Union said.
